tests.name: aggregates
tests.description: The Aggregates section: aggregate() with $this, $index and $total in the aggregator, init given, omitted and empty, an empty input, an aggregator returning empty or more than one item, the worked examples of 2.0.0 and 3.0.0, where 3.0.0 evaluates init and how it nests; and 3.0.0's sum(), min(), max() and avg() (3.0.0 only): the types each takes, the result type, an empty input, and items of different types. Comparison and arithmetic are covered by equality-comparison.xml and math.xml and are cited here only where a case needs them. Leaves out what the text does not settle: an init of more than one item under 2.0.0 (init : value), $total used outside aggregate() or inside init, items of a type a function does not list (a Boolean to any of them, a String to sum or avg, a Date to sum), whether "SHALL be the same type" in sum, min, max and avg is judged before or after implicit conversion (Integer with Decimal, Integer or Decimal with Quantity, Date with DateTime), Quantities in different units, items of the same type that do not compare (dates of different precision, incommensurable units), the unit of a sum or average of quantities with different units, Integer overflow in sum, the precision of an avg result, and Long items (5L), which the pinned grammar does not parse.

group.name: REQ-AGGREGATES-001
group.description: aggregate evaluates the aggregator for each item with $this set to the item, $total starts at init and takes the aggregator's result after every iteration, and the result is $total after the last iteration
group.source: Performs general-purpose aggregation by evaluating the aggregator expression for each element of the input collection. Within this expression, the standard iteration variables of `$this` and `$index` can be accessed, but also a `$total` aggregation variable.
The value of the `$total` variable is set to `init`, or empty (`{ }`) if no `init` value is supplied, and is set to the result of the aggregator expression after every iteration.
For the <<aggregates,aggregate>> function, expressions may also refer to the special `$total` element, representing the result of the aggregation.

Performs general-purpose aggregation by evaluating the aggregator expression for each item of the input collection. Within this expression, the standard iteration variables of `$this` and `$index` can be accessed, but also a `$total` aggregation variable.
The result of the aggregate function is the value of `$total` after the last iteration.
Ordered - The order of items in the collection is important and is preserved through operations as much as possible.

The value of the `$total` variable is set to `init`, or empty (`{ }`) if no `init` value is supplied, and is set to the result of the aggregator expression after every iteration.

The `init` argument is evaluated once at the start to initialize the `$total` variable.
The `aggregator` argument is then evaluated for each item (setting `$this`and `$index` for each), and has access to the current value of `$total` available. The result of the evaluation is then assigned to `$total`.
The final value of `$total` is returned as the result of the function.

group.name: REQ-AGGREGATES-011
group.description: init is evaluated on the outer context, so $this in init is the outer $this (3.0.0 only; 2.0.0 does not say where init is evaluated)
group.source: The `init` argument is evaluated once before setting `$this` and `$index`, so will be evaluated on the outer context, and will have access to outer `$this` values.

group.name: REQ-AGGREGATES-012
group.description: A nested aggregate has its own $total and $this; once it completes, the outer $total and $this are available again (3.0.0 only)
group.source: Variables introduced by scoped functions can only be accessed within the specified parameters of the scoped function. This behavior is preserved through nesting, meaning specifically that once a nested scope function evaluation is complete, the variables in the outer scoped function are again available.
Holds the running total during processing, and at the end will be the result returned by the function.
